proposals.evidence: DEDR3098 explicitly gives Tamil/Malayalam tā(r)- give with tā imperative and the same first/second-person giving meaning in Badaga. Betta Kurumba tara and Irula tā give are comparative continuations of that giving stem; retain the elicited general give gloss without inventing a specified recipient. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4205 gives Tamil piṉ, Malayalam pimpu, Kota pibal/piga·r and Kannada pinde/him behind. These southern pin-/pimp-/pih-/in(d)- survey responses retain the documented back/behind stem with ordinary locative extensions and regular Kannada-area loss of initial p/h. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2668 gives Tamil cutti/cuttiyal, Malayalam cutti/cuttika, Kannada suttige, Tulu sutti/suttè, Telugu sutte and Gondi sutte hammer. These survey cut-/sut- hammer responses retain the attested family and ordinary suffixes. The article also compares Marathi sutkī; this external comparison is retained as a caveat and does not establish an immediate donor for these forms. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
